title: Implement staff principals and initial provisioning

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Staff principal tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/staff_access/test_principals.py

verify.summary: Fresh T3 verification passed both configured gates and two independent isolated provisioning probes. The probes proved normalized uniqueness, stdin and hidden-prompt provisioning, independent Argon2id verification, output/service-log redaction, single-head migration, safe rerun and complete task-owned cleanup without crossing Staff Access ownership or anti-goals.

Independent T3 verification (verifier-owned project face-moment-task003-verify1) reran all task gates (mypy 18 files, focused pytest 1 passed, single alembic head 0002_staff_users) and proved FT-001-AC-006 with a fresh 32-check probe: migration round-trip, strip+casefold normalized unique active photographer, only Argon2id hash persisted and independently verified via argon2-cffi, hidden-prompt and stdin intake without echo, redacted output and service logs, argon2-cffi 25.1.0 confirmed on PyPI, complete task-owned cleanup with Docker restored inactive.

Fresh adversarial semantic review challenged secret intake and error paths, normalized uniqueness, Argon2id-only persistence, transaction rollback, model/migration equivalence, ownership, anti-goals, safe rerun and cleanup; no finding or operator question survived.
The explicit manual lifecycle owner closed TASK-003 after independent functional PASS and per-task semantic-pass satisfied all T3 obligations.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-006 RED: an owner cannot provision an active photographer through the canonical path, so no normalized unique principal with a verifiable Argon2id credential exists; GREEN: one disposable photographer is provisioned with a normalized unique username and only an Argon2id hash persisted while supplied-secret and stored-hash markers remain absent from command output and application logs; decisive comparison: repository/authentication observations satisfy the principal contract and redaction scan finds no protected marker; artifact: redacted CLI/repository test output and database projection.
purpose: Create the minimum owner-backed staff identity and initial credential path required before the photographer can authenticate.
success_outcome: An owner can provision an active photographer principal whose normalized identity and Argon2id credential persist in the shared schema without exposing the supplied password or stored hash.
anti_goals: Do not implement browser sessions, password reset, deactivation or Photo authorization.
Do not add self-registration, password-recovery email, OAuth, MFA, a generic IAM service or production seed identities.

forbidden_scope: Photo admission, processing and serving-target behavior
Production identities, secrets or deployment actions
stop_conditions: Provisioning would require changing the accepted staff roles or authentication architecture.
Passing the task would require storing, echoing or logging plaintext credentials.
Work expands into session, reset/deactivation or business authorization outcomes owned by sibling tasks.

constraints: staff_access owns principal and credential persistence under src/face_moment/platform/auth/.
The migration uses the single shared Base and linear Alembic stream; its direct down_revision is the current head at execution.
The command accepts secrets without echoing them and persists only Argon2id encoded hashes.
invariants: Only photographer, operator and developer are valid staff roles.
Plaintext passwords and stored password hashes never enter URLs or application logs.
Initial provisioning creates no browser session or Photo-domain state.
verification_targets: Isolated migration/repository/CLI proof covers provision success, normalized uniqueness, Argon2id verification and redaction with task-owned cleanup.
